t: You're in Pembridge Square, a residential square in Bayswater, close to Notting Hill. It was laid out in the nineteenth century by the landowner Robert Hall, with the builders Francis and William Radford, and built between 1858 and 1864. Look for the stucco frontages, and note that several buildings here are Grade II listed. Winifred Cullis died here in 1956. She was a physiologist, and the first woman to hold a professorial chair at a medical school.
